reasoning: The evidence shows South Korea's total fertility rate (TFR) increased from 0.72 in 2023 to 0.75 in 2024, exceeding the 0.72 threshold. Multiple 2025 data points indicate continued growth: Q2 2025 TFR reached 0.76, July 2025 reached 0.80, and births have risen for 13+ consecutive months with 7.2-7.4% year-over-year growth in early 2025. Experts project 2025 TFR could reach 0.8. The rebound is driven by increased marriages, larger cohorts of women in their 30s, and changing attitudes toward childbirth. While structural challenges remain (late maternal age, low multi-child births), the trajectory strongly suggests 2025 TFR will exceed 0.72.
